doc.title: Ann Rabson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 21, 2007

title: Hearing Big Bill Broonzy on the radio at age four
summary: At four she heard Broonzy live on Purdue's radio station and was transformed; Studs Terkel later dated it 1949, and her father encouraged her.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Let me just rewind a little bit. I’ve read a couple of times that you credit Big Bill Broonzy with like this a-ha moment or something.
It was very much, what do they call it, an epiphany or something?

I was four years old and I heard live on the radio, a college radio, Purdue’s radio station, I heard Big Bill Broonzy playing live on the radio. And I was just blown away. I mean I’d heard lots of music in my home, but it was like this was my music. It was like, and he was singing, you know looking back I know, one of the songs he sang was “I’m Going to Move Way Out on the Outskirts of Town.” And I know that as a kid you can’t really understanding the sort of sexual innuendo and all that. But what came through to me was the loneliness and powerlessness. And I mean I was four years old. I had those feelings. And it really gave me goose bumps. I mean it really changed my life. I always thought I was five years old and it was 1950. But later in life, like a couple of years ago, I met Studs Turkel. And we were talking and he asked me, you know he was great interviewer. He asked me when did I first hear blues. And I told him and he said, “Oh no,” he said, “that wasn’t 1950” he said, “That was 1949 and I was with him on that trip.”
Yeah. So you know, that was that.
I’ll be. That’s a neat coincidence. Were you able to go to — who could you go to in your family, or whatever, and you’re four years old and like try to share this feeling?

My father. Absolutely. My father was so excited that I was excited about music. He went out and got records and showed me — he could play boogie woogie and showed me some of that, and definitely. I mean my brother and I were not on real good terms much in my childhood. And my mom was, you know, she was really busy and stuff. But my dad, he was really the one who encouraged me, and is still encouraging me.
